# GEO report: acme-mugs **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. All results below are read from code. I ran no live check because no URL was given. ## Code score: 24–33/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 5.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 24. High = (5.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 33. The site tells every crawler to stay out, and it is a browser-only React app, so its pages arrive as an empty shell. Those two problems account for most of the lost points. The only unknown is the canonical link, because no site domain is declared anywhere. I found no `geo.config.json`, so I assumed you want search and AI search tools to find this site. The 40-point cap for a blocker applied (a search crawler is blocked site-wide), but the score is already below 40. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking all crawlers in robots.txt - **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` asks every crawler, including Googlebot, Bingbot and the AI search crawlers, to read nothing on the site. This is a blocker, and it also makes your pages count as blocked under GEO-014. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:2` - **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 50–59. GEO-009 and GEO-014 both become Clear, which adds 6 points. ### 2. Put page content in the HTML the server sends - **Why it matters:** Many crawlers don't run JavaScript. They currently see only `
`, so they miss the headings and text of both pages. The catalogue is also fetched in the browser. - **Where:** `index.html:8`, `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:6` - **What the code says:** `
` and `fetch('/api/mugs')` inside `useEffect` - **Size:** Large. Use prerendering or SSR (for example a prerender plugin, or a move to a framework like Next.js or Astro), and load the catalogue data at build or server time. - **Score after this:** 37–46 ### 3. Give pages a real title, description and language - **Why it matters:** Every page currently shows the placeholder title "Vite App", with no description and no `lang`. - **Where:** `index.html:2` and `index.html:5` - **What the code says:** `` and `Vite App` - **Size:** Small. Set `lang="en"` and add a meta description. Per-route titles need a head helper such as `react-helmet-async`, and they only reach crawlers once item 2 is done. - **Score after this:** 33–41 ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and within limits | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is plain, valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:2`, `Disallow: /` under `User-agent: *`. Site-wide. | | GEO-014 | Linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:2` blocks Googlebot and Bingbot on `/` and `/catalogue` (0 of 2 routes clear). No noindex found. | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your domain | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical in `index.html`, and no domain is declared. Which domain should it be? | | GEO-003 | Content present in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `index.html:8` empty root, no prerendering (0 of 2 routes clear). | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is in robots.txt | Problem | Not run | No sitemap file, and no `Sitemap:` line in `public/robots.txt` | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | Not run | `index.html:2` has no `lang`, `index.html:5` has `Vite App`, and there is no meta description (0 of 2 routes clear). | | GEO-016 | Key routes reachable via real links | Problem | Not run | `src/main.jsx:11`, ``. `/catalogue` has no ``. | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet` in `index.html`, and no middleware or header config in the repo | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Problem | Not run | `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`, `` has no `alt`. `Catalogue` is clear (1 of 2 routes). I read both pages and the `Nav` component. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (informational) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. This is optional and not scored. | | GEO-102 | App structured data (informational) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app. Not scored. | ## Other problems found - `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`: `` has no `alt` text. Fix: add a short description, for example `alt="Handmade ceramic mugs"`. This is the same finding as GEO-002. - Nothing else found. ## Can't tell from code - **GEO-015 (canonical):** No site domain is declared. Tell me your domain (or add `site.origin` to `geo.config.json`) and I can settle this. If you add a canonical, it must be one absolute URL per page. - **GEO-003:** If your host prerenders pages outside this repository, the result could change. A live scan would confirm what crawlers actually receive. - **GEO-011:** The sitemap's listed URLs can't be checked until a sitemap exists. - **Bot protection:** Code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs `, which compares real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Training crawlers:** Your policy on `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` is separate from search access. The current `*` block covers them too, and it isn't scored. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. If the `Disallow: /` is deliberate (for example a staging site), tell me and GEO-009 and GEO-014 would change. - The `/api/mugs` data is loaded from a backend I can't see. - `index.html` is the only HTML shell, with no hosting-level prerendering. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
